caption:
When I was pregnant, I had no idea if I’d even be able to breastfeed. I knew I wanted to try, but I also knew it doesn’t always work out the way you hope.

My milk didn’t come in for 5 days. Those 5 days felt long. I remember wondering if it was ever going to happen.

It also took several days for Zy to latch. We saw multiple lactation consultants, and every single one had a different opinion. Looking back, I’m grateful for that. I took a little piece from each person and found what worked best for us.

When I set my goal, I picked 6 months.

That felt realistic while running a business, opening a gym, and being the working parent. I knew it would require planning. I knew it would be “inconvenient” at times and that I’d have to intentionally build my days around it.

What I didn’t expect... was how much I would love it.

There’s something so intimate about it. So grounding. So beautifully human... and so animalistic.

I feel really grateful that we took our trip to Tanzania before Zy was born. Watching zebras, giraffes, elephants, and lions all caring for and feeding their babies changed something in me. At the time, I didn’t fully understand why I felt so connected to it. Now I do.

There is something incredibly grounding about realizing that mothers, across so many species, have been nourishing and protecting their babies long before us. It makes motherhood feel both incredibly ordinary and incredibly miraculous at the same time. Sometimes I wonder if that trip happened exactly when it was supposed to.

It’s wild to think that his little body has been built from mine.

As someone who has dedicated my career to health, breastfeeding has given me another appreciation for nutrition. Knowing that everything I eat is nourishing him has made me even more intentional. Watching food become fuel for another tiny human is one of the coolest things I’ve ever experienced.

It has also given me so much more appreciation for every mom who breastfeeds—whether it’s for a few days, a few weeks, a few months, or a few years.

caption:
OMFG WE DID ITTTTTTTTT!!!!!!!!!!! STANDING ON THE HIGHEST POINT IN AFRICA! 

On Day 6, we went to bed at 2:00 PM after a full morning of hiking, knowing we’d need to wake up at 11:00 PM to eat and begin our summit push.

12:30 AM – Our ascent began. Summit sits at 19,500 feet — the cruising altitude of some planes.

Halfway up, we stopped for ginger tea to watch the sunrise. 🥹

Midway, Jahmeek got altitude sickness — energy gone, throwing up. For a split second, I wondered if we’d have to stop. But the mantra is “pole pole” (slowly, slowly). Step by step, we pushed forward. 🗻

7:30 AM – Peak 1.
8:30 AM – Uhuru Peak — the highest point in Africa.

One foot after another, repeating:
Tough times are temporary.
We can do hard things.
No regrets.

After 9 hours up, it was time to descend — another 5 hours down. Fastest and longest day of my life. Once we got back to basecamp, we immediately passed out for a nap, ate lunch, then started another 3-hour trek to our final camp. After a great night’s sleep, we finished the mountain with 5 hours down the final steps of the mountain.

Couldn’t have done it without Ami, Doudi, Musa, and Abasi. We celebrated with a feast, cake, and certificates. Jahmeek said, “I’m framing this.” 🙋🏼‍♀️🙋🏿

Kili is no joke. MAD respect for anyone who’s done it.

Vlog of our 8 days + lessons learned to come! 🫶

➡️ You can do hard things.
➡️ Tough moments don’t last.
➡️ One foot after another.
➡️ No regrets.

caption:
Where do I even begin with the last three weeks?

They have been the most beautiful, grounding, heart-expanding — and wildly educational days.

From pregnancy, to labour, to birth, to suddenly becoming parents — it’s been a whole world of NEW. New cries. Cluster feeds. Hunger cues. How often babies poop. Discovering that gas is an entire personality trait early on 😂. The importance of constant body contact. Umbilical cord care. That nail clipping is low-key terrifying at first. Safe sleep practices. The learning curve has been STEEP and constant, and I’m SO thankful for everyone who’s been there to answer my 1000s of questions (you know who you are 🫶🏼).

There’s been learning in recovery too — how to care for my body after birth and trust that healing isn’t linear or meant to be rushed.

I’ve left the house 5x in three weeks. My step count is under 200 a day. And as someone whose identity is deeply rooted in coaching, movement, and life in the gym, I’m honestly proud of myself for surrendering to healing. Also very grateful it’s cold and snowy (sorry everyone lol) because there’s zero FOMO — recovering from an episiotomy in the summer would be a whole different experience 😂.

Somehow, instincts have been quietly kicking in. Why is it that at 3am, running on broken sleep, I feel so calm and capable? I don’t fully understand it — but I feel it.

Our days have been full of cuddles. Of slowing down. Of doing “nothing”… but somehow everything. Feeding, rocking, staring, just being. Life has softened in a way I didn’t expect.

At 3am during one of our feeds this week, I thought to myself: as two people who love adventure as much as we do, we’ve truly stepped into the greatest one yet.

It’s been incredible to watch our teamwork unfold. Learning how to care for ourselves, each other, and this tiny human — all while everything feels new and unknown. I’m endlessly grateful to be spending these days with Jahmeek, and my heart holds so much respect for solo parents navigating this season.

Now brb while I go sing Ziah to sleep (with a Christmas song)… because I don’t know any nursery rhymes yet 😂🤍

caption:
Moments I Never Want to Forget 🤍

I never want to forget your dad’s face when I showed him the pregnancy test.

Climbing Gros Morne with you inside of me—5.5 months pregnant, feeling strong, capable, and in my body.

Lying on the bed in Shediac with your dad and feeling your very first kick 🥲

Sharing the news and hearing, “Of course we knew—we were just waiting for you to tell us.” Apparently it was somewhat obvious lol.

Our ultrasound. The tech asking me to jump around to get you to move… and me casually breaking out a handstand.

Making national television when we climbed the CN Tower together at 8 months pregnant.

Our quiet time before you arrived—on the couch, early to bed, hands on my belly, feeling your kicks and movements🤰 

The day my water broke, and the pure excitement in your dad’s eyes 🥹

Our labour. Our strength. Putting hypnobirthing into practice.
The moment you were placed on my stomach. Your dad cutting your cord. Lying there together while time stood still.

The OB yelling, “THAT’S A TODDLER!” as you came out of me. ☠️

The way your Dad completely ignored that I didn’t want a middle name and fit his right in there for you 😆

You passing your hearing test—and your dad saving the paper like it was a trophy 😂

Trying to dress you in a swaggy adidas outfit to leave the hospital… only to end up right back in a sleeper 🙃

Our walk out of the hospital. Our drive home. Walking into the house as three. 🫶🏼🫶🏿

All of January—surrendering.
Learning you.
Learning each other.
Learning us.

The hair on your head. Your big feet. The scrunched cheeks and rolls everywhere. Your newborn sounds. 👶🏽

The first time you peed on me. TYSM.

Pouring warm water over your head during your first bath 🛁 

The way your dad and I celebrated when we fed you back to your birth weight—LOL, IYKYK.

The way our family and friends have shown up for us 😭

The way your dad showed up for me—my stitches, my body, feeding me so I could feed you. 😭😭

Late nights—
11pm, 1am, 3am, 5am, 7am—on repeat.
Weirdly not tired.
Figuring it out together.

I never want to forget the little moments shaping us into parents.

caption:
Never stop learning.
As a coach.
As a client.

Be curious.

Because the moment you think you know everything is the moment you stop growing.

Curiosity keeps you open.
It helps you ask better questions, notice the details, and continue evolving—both in your coaching and in your training.

And growth happens even faster when you surround yourself with people who are committed to it too.

A team.
Mentors.
Peers who challenge you, support you, and push you to be better.

Because iron sharpens iron.

And sometimes, the biggest improvements come from the things we overlook…

Everyone’s out here chasing bigger biceps, glutes, and a 6-pack…

Meanwhile I’m over here thinking—

What’s really sexy?

A foot, rib cage, and pelvis that function optimally.
(Seriously lol)

Because your feet are packed with over 200,000 sensory receptors—constantly sending information to your brain to control posture, balance, and movement.

This is your foundation.

In the gym and in daily life:
– Can you feel your connection to the ground?
– Are you building a strong foot tripod?

Think:
Big toe. Pinky toe. Heel.
Three points of contact working together to create stability and support.

When your foundation is strong, everything above it has the potential to be stronger too.

Don’t forget about your feet.

In pregnancy and postpartum, this is often linked with diastasis recti abdominis (DRA), when the linea alba has been stretched and thinned. However, coning is not always “bad” - it’s simply a sign that the body is not managing pressure optimally in that moment. When you see coning, it’s essentially your body’s way of saying:

“This movement is more than my core system can currently control.” or “My pressure management strategy isn’t effective here.”

Not confidence from achievements — but confidence from evidence. Evidence that we do what we say we’ll do. That we can do hard things.

This is how identity shifts. This is how resilience is built.
And this is why we keep choosing the hard path — not to prove anything to anyone else… but to become the kind of people we want to be.

The course helped me understand that many recurring issues people experience aren’t just local—they’re systemic. And the feet are often the starting point. 🦶

We hiked 8 hours yesterday, slept at a higher altitude, and I woke up feeling rough — blue lips, pounding head, and a fever. Thankful Jahmeek feels 100% fine so he can take care of me LOL.

Today’s route from Shira Camp 2 to Baranco was supposed to be 10km in about 6 hours, but we took a 2.5-hour detour to avoid the crowds on the steep rocks. In hindsight, I should have used that time to rest — the cave was stunning, but the hike was HARD and completely off course. My lower body really felt it. 😆

The final two hours were relentless — an hour straight down the mountain, only to climb right back up to camp. We finished hiking at 6 PM and were in bed by 7 PM — completely wiped.

Scroll to see me near the end of the day, barely able to keep my eyes open. Oh, and we witnessed our third rescue in five days — this mountain is no joke.

Today was hard, but that’s what we’re here for. We knew Day 5 would test us. Just kept telling myself: tough moments never last.

Thank to @champagnepapi for getting us through the last hour of this. 🙏🏼 Safe to say every Tanzanian we have met has downloaded Nokia. 😜

When people say, “I’ll do that when I retire” or “I’m saving that for later,” I always want to say, how do you know you’ll make it to retirement? And even then, who knows what your health will look like. So, three weeks ago, Jahmeek and I were chatting about our plans—discussing if and when we’ll try again for another baby and when I’d resume looking for a new gym space (I put it on hold in the fall with everything). In that moment, I turned to him and said, “We’re going to hike Kili.” And in very Jahmeek fashion, he says “YA WE ARE”. 🏔️

Yes, three weeks ago we decided we were going to fly to Tanzania and hike the highest mountain there. THIS IS WHY I HAVE TRAINED FOR THE LAST 15 YEARS… so I can say YES to every adventure life brings at any time. 🏋️‍♂️ 

My motto has always been “no regrets.” That twinge of regret I felt was a clear sign: the time is now.

I took a photo in the same part of the airport a decade ago when I was heading to Asia for a six-month trip after my brother passed away. And now here I am again, on the biggest adventure of my life, I feel not only SO ALIVE and also so close to him. 🤗

We’re off to do some epic stuff—an eight-day hike up the tallest mountain in Africa. Here we come!

Three little Cassie lessons for ya 😘 
1. No regrets 
2. Don’t wait for later
3. Lift weights and do mobility. Be strong and mobile so you can physically do all the things you want to do!

Jahmeek and I have been together for almost 14 years, and regularly checking in on our well-being has made a huge difference in our lives. These 10 questions help us stay aligned and support each other’s growth:

1. How do you feel about where you’re at right now?
2. What do you want for yourself?
3. Do you feel supported in pursuing what you want for yourself?
4. How many days per week would you ideally like to exercise, and how can I support that goal?
5. Which foods make you feel your best, and how can we enjoy them together?
6. What sleep schedule helps you feel rested—when do you want to go to bed and wake up?
7. What does rest mean to you?
8. What excites you, and how can we invite more of that into our lives?
9. What adventures do you want to experience together, and when can we schedule them into our lives?
10. What solo adventures do you dream about, and how can I support you in making them happen?

What other questions do you find valuable to reflect on with your partner? 🙋🏼‍♀️🙋🏿

Taking time to reflect on these questions can strengthen both your individual well-being and your relationship. I’ve been a personal trainer and coach for over a decade, and I’ve seen first hand how having a supportive partner can be a game changer when you’re striving for a happy, healthy and fulfilled life—if your partner isn’t in your corner, achieving your wants and goals becomes a lot tougher. 🫶

Also, not to offer unsolicited relationship advice but if I had a partner who wasn’t supportive with what I wanted in my life, I would say GTFO 😂✌🏼life is too short to be held back or out of alignment.

caption:
10 years ago, I lost my little brother, and that deep grief taught me to guard my heart, to protect myself from the possibility of more pain. So, when we became pregnant, I held back on fully embracing the joy, as if preparing myself for the ‘just in case’. Looking back, that realization itself makes me feel sad—to think that fear of loss kept me from fully embracing the joy.

By week 9, I began to feel excited about starting the next chapter of our life, becoming parents together. Then, at week 12, everything quickly changed. We got the call that we were high-risk, and the next day, the bleeding started. Two days later, I was in the emergency room, experiencing a pain that NO ONE prepares you for—both physical and emotional. I’ve never felt pain like this before. (I’ll spare you the details that started in Farm Boy lol.)

Miscarriage is rarely talked about, and we’re often told not to share pregnancy news until we’re ‘in the clear’ after 12 weeks. I thought I’d share immediately, but when it happened, I didn’t tell anyone and asked Jahmeek to do the same. If it hadn’t been for two friends who’d openly shared their experiences with me, I would have felt truly alone. That’s why I’m sharing this now. It’s been a tough 10 days, and I’m grateful for the people who understand. I can’t imagine going through this alone, and I hope by speaking out, others might feel less alone too.

The biggest takeaway has been realizing how much healing is required through loss. Even though my little brother passed a decade ago, and I feel like I’ve ‘done the work,’ his loss will always impact me. Grief is complex, and healing isn’t linear. I used to think time would make me move past it—but the truth is, the work of healing never truly ends, and that’s okay.

Through this recent loss, I’ve learned that I don’t want to live in fear. I want to live fully. To do that, I know I need to keep checking in with myself—my emotions, my choices, and my actions. Loss has taught me so much about love, resilience, self-compassion, and the importance of living with an open heart.

If you’re going through something similar, know that you’re not alone, and that we don’t have to walk alone. 🫶🫶

caption:
Scroll right to see bb 2012 Cassie 12 years ago when I was last in Barcelona 👀 

📍Barcelona Trip - 4 day itinerary 

🏨 Hotel in Gothic Quarter (old town) - in the thick of it, walkable distance to everywhere allowed us to both get our steps in and save on taxis. @cataloniahotels

Day 1 - Tourist for the day!
- Arrived
- Bike tour with @getyourguide 
- Paella making class with @getyourguide 
Crashed from time change. 💤 

Day 2 - Tourist for the day!
- all the tourist sites in a 7 hour tour @viator (Sagrada Familia, Park Güell, Guided tour at Gothic Quarter and Montjuic Hill)
- Dinner at @brugarolbarcelona EXCEPTIONAL! 
- Sips voted #1 bar in the world (how cute is my bubble mocktail!!!) 

Day 3 - Local for the day! 
- Slept in 
- Went for brunch @tranqui.cafe.bcn (Healthy/Cute)
- Walked around to the shops and neighbour shops 
- Beach boardwalk + Sunset Boat Cruise 
- Went out for dinner @TerrazaMartinez
- Bed early 💤 

Day 4 - Locals for the day!
- Walk to brunch @thecoffeehousebcn (Healthy/Cute)
- Walked around through neighbourhoods
- Lunch @honestgreens (Healthy/Fast Casual)
- Evening flight ✈️ 

You could definitely do Barcelona is 2-3 days, but I highly encourage 3-4. Those extra days that we chilled made me Fall in love with Barcelona.🥹 Typically we hit the gym everywhere we go, it’s one of my favourite ways to feel like a local. However, we didn’t have any luck finding a gym near by with day passes available. One of my favourite parts about travelling though is how much walking you do. We may have not hit the gym, but easily did 15k steps everyday. Body, mind and heart are FEELING GOOD! 🥰

Is the person you’re with contributing to the lifestyle you want for yourself? For us, it’s a crucial part of our personal growth and the health of our relationship.

Questions we often check in on:
1. Do we share similar values?

3. Are our daily habits and routines compatible?

5. Do we provide the emotional support one another needs?

caption:
In the past 12 years, we’ve always chosen experiences over possessions. Instead of holiday and anniversary gifts, we’ve done adventures, shared moments, and new discoveries that have brought us so much joy. Each experience deepens our connection, fuels our growth, and creates memories that shape who we are. 🫶🫶

PARIS DAY 1, RUNDOWN ⬇️

📍We stayed in the 4th arrondissement to be within walking distance of everything. With such a short trip, we didn’t want to waste time commuting.

We started with coffee and pain au chocolat at a cafe near our hotel before taking an Uber to the Palace of Versailles. We booked a two-hour tour with @getyourguide to skip the line and gain a deeper understanding of what we were seeing.

Back in the city, we joined a four-hour city bike tour—an awesome way to stay active, see the sights, and learn the history behind each landmark.

Next, we took a serene 9:45pm cruise, a stunning way to see the city at night. Being on the water gives you a whole new perspective.

We finished the night with escargot and French onion soup (just “onion soup” in France!).

And with that, Paris officially takes the #1 spot in my heart over New York City.

Let me know below if you want a rundown on Day 2. 😊

caption:
Day trip from Bucharest to Transylvania for a little country side and adventure! First stop: Dracula’s Castle (a.k.a. Bran Castle), built in the 14th century as a fortress to defend against invading forces. Now, it’s famous for its spooky Dracula lore. 🧛 We explored the twisty staircases, secret rooms, and Jahmeek insisted I include the torture chamber (last photo). 🫣

Next, we went to Peles Castle, built in the late 19th century as a summer retreat for Romania’s first king, King Carol I. It’s GORGEOUS neo-renaissance architecture and royal charm. It’s intricate woodwork, grand halls, and history blew us away.

Jahmeek’s line of the day: “Now, I truly understand what they mean when they say, ‘Live like a king.’” 🤴🏿
